title: Annual Large Bank Capital Requirements - Federal Reserve Board
summary: This Federal Reserve page explains the capital framework for large bank holding companies ($100B+ assets) but functions as a navigation hub. It describes how CET1 requirements are calculated (4.5% minimum + SCB + G-SIB surcharge) but does NOT contain actual 2025 capital numbers — those are in the linked 2025 Large Bank Capital Requirements PDF.
key_points: Covered institutions include bank holding companies, covered savings and loan holding companies, and U.S. intermediate holding companies with $100 billion or more in total consolidated assets

Total CET1 capital ratio requirement is composed of: minimum 4.5% CET1 ratio (identical for all banks), stress capital buffer (SCB) of at least 2.5% based on supervisory stress test results, and if applicable, a G-SIB capital surcharge of at least 1.0%
Page serves as an index linking to annual requirement PDFs (2020–2025) rather than presenting the actual capital numbers
Category IV firms generally not required to participate in supervisory stress test in odd years, though 2025 required their participation
why_it_matters: The capital framework is foundational to banking regulation, but this page provides no quantitative data. The SCB methodology creates a feedback loop between stress test results and capital buffers. Market participants need the actual PDF (not this page) for specific 2025 capital requirement figures.
market_structure_context: This describes the Federal Reserve's supervisory capital architecture for large banks, which is regulatory framework rather than actionable market structure data. The substantive capital numbers for 2025 are in the linked PDF, not this index page.
